title: Deceptive-intent contrast screen: target-token activations on 36 hand-written contrast pairs plus 12 fillers
procedure: This is a neuron SEARCH, not a test of a named candidate: no neuron is claimed in advance. L20-N1234 is listed only because it is a required control (below); the measurement is atlas-wide. Run one forward pass per prompt in prompts.json in requests/deceptive-intent-contrast-001/ (84 prompts, 11 to 28 Marin tokens each, every prompt carrying exactly one [[marked]] target token, the word that completes the claim). For each prompt, record the MLP neuron activation silu(gate)*up at the marked token position for every neuron in every layer, and return the full table (prompt id, layer, neuron, activation) plus run metadata (model revision, precision). No generation, no steering, no ablation. The fleet then scores, locally and with the same machinery as its capybara pair screen: per neuron and per contrast, the pair-direction rate and mean high-minus-low difference at the marked token; greedy coalitions up to 16 units; and, per layer, 100 random neurons scored identically as the baseline distribution. Fillers are scored as a no-contrast sanity arm. The pairs implement three pre-registered contrasts, 12 pairs each: (1) enacted deception vs honest persuasion on matched topics; (2) enacted deception vs narrated deception (news, court, case-study, and other frames, varied on purpose); (3) deliberate lie vs sincere falsehood, where both arms state the same claim and only the writer's knowledge differs, and every sincere arm is confident and uncorrected. Pairs were written and tokenizer-checked before any activation was seen on them; targets are the same Marin token within each pair (verified in the source file). Label rules and per-pair annotations ship in DESIGN.md.
prediction: Pre-registered before any run, 2026-11-12: (a) no single neuron passes all three contrasts; if anything passes, it is a coalition of 16 or fewer units. (b) The control L20-N1234 (the minced-oath / register neuron) fails all three contrasts; if it passes, the screen is measuring register or urgency, not intent, and the run is void. (c) If 5 or more of the 100 random same-layer neurons pass all three contrasts for any layer, the screen is too loose and the run is inconclusive regardless of any candidate.
pass_rule: A candidate (single neuron or coalition up to 16) passes only if it clears all three contrasts: in each contrast the predicted (high) arm's summed activation exceeds the low arm's in at least 80 percent of the 12 pairs, AND the mean pair difference beats the 95th percentile of the 100 random same-layer neurons scored the same way. The headline result is the smallest passing set. A read-side pass licenses only a follow-on causal request (type B for a single neuron, type E for a coalition); it is not by itself a claim that the set decides anything.
refuted_if: No single neuron and no coalition up to 16 clears all three contrasts while the controls behave (L20-N1234 failing, fewer than 5 of 100 random neurons passing). That outcome is a clean null and will be reported as one: it would mean deceptive intent is not a small localized MLP coalition recoverable by this method, or that these labels do not isolate it. It would not prove Marin has no representation of deception; the feature could live in attention, in a residual direction, or in a larger set.
compute: 84 forward passes of at most 28 tokens (about 1,700 tokens total), no generation. The only heavy part is capturing all MLP activations at one marked position per prompt.
outputs: One CSV or JSON table: prompt id, contrast/arm or filler id, layer, neuron, activation at the marked token; plus model revision and precision. The fleet publishes its scoring either way, pass or null.
